context: Decide per symbol rather than uniformly. For each of the three, either (a) promote to a public name -- drop the underscore, give it a docstring stating its contract, and add a row to docs/reference/public-contracts.md if it is genuinely part of the core surface MCP and CLI both depend on -- or (b) keep it private, remove it from __all__, and give the surfaces a public wrapper that expresses the intended seam. _resolve_mode_with_registry is the one with a live cross-package consumer, so it is the strongest candidate for promotion. Note the whole-program layering stays green either way; this is about naming honesty, not import structure.
description: Verified at develop 29380ce9e. benchbox/core/run_service.py declares __all__ containing three private names: _translate_platform_options_for_adapter, _resolve_mode_with_registry, and _map_phases_to_execution_type. The underscore says internal; membership in __all__ says public API. Both cannot be true, and the contradiction is load-bearing rather than cosmetic: benchbox/mcp/tools/benchmark.py:274 does 'from benchbox.core.run_service import _resolve_mode_with_registry', a cross-package import of a private symbol. This is how the MCP run-service adoption was made to work -- by widening the seam to expose the helpers MCP needed instead of promoting them to real public names with a considered signature. The adoption itself is genuine and verified (execute_run is called at benchmark.py:483, the three MCP-side translators are gone, run_with_platform is no longer used, lint-imports reports 3 contracts kept and 0 broken, and the cross-surface equivalence rung passes). The risk is to the NEXT extraction rather than to current behavior: the module no longer states which of its symbols carry a stability promise, so a future change cannot tell what it is allowed to break. docs/reference/public-contracts.md is the repository's mechanism for exactly this question and does not currently cover these names.

preserves.behavior: MCP keeps executing through execute_run; this is a rename and contract-documentation change, not a re-plumbing of the adoption.
lint-imports stays green: core still imports neither platforms nor cli, and mcp still never imports cli.
